title: "Virtual Icechunk"
subtitle: "A short tutorial for the 2026 IOOS Hackathon"

This tutorial gives you a quick overview of virtual Icechunk stores: what they
are, how one gets built, and what to check before building one. During the
hackathon you will mostly hand the actual work to a coding agent that has the
[ocean-icechunks-skills](https://github.com/ocean-icechunks/ocean-icechunks-skills)
installed. Each chapter is a short slide deck. Click through it, or press **S**
for the speaker notes.

## Start here: two quick wins

1. **Open 306 TB in about a second.** Bering Sea bottom temperature on the snow
   crab grounds, 1994–2015, from the HYCOM reanalysis.
   [Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/ocean-icechunks/hycom/blob/main/hycom-gofs-3pt1-reanalysis/bering-sea-snow-crab-demo.ipynb)
2. **Make your own virtual store.** Five NOAA NDVI files on AWS become one
   local Icechunk store.
   [Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/ocean-icechunks/2026-ioos-hackathon/blob/main/notebooks/simple-virtual-icechunk.ipynb)
